messages:
sam: Heads-up — we're planning to change the /v1/generate default model when `model` is omitted. This will switch the unpinned default alias to a newer 70B quant variant. Need quick alignment on whether this counts as breaking and how we communicate. Questions: 1) treat as non-breaking with warnings or explicit breaking? 2) timeline for alias + SDK warnings? 3) comms plan for customers and enterprise? @maria @liam @anya

maria: Don’t want surprises for customers. My knee-jerk: add a version header + deprecation notice header, and a short public changelog entry now. Proposed: X-Model-Version + X-Deprecation-Notice header. Also recommend a 6-week opt-in period where old default alias still works. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

liam: Runtime notes: changing default may change latency profiles and the KV cache hit rate but not the core response JSON shape. However max_sequence and tokenization differences could affect downstream token-cost reporting. For pinned customers nothing changes. Mitigation: keep `default-old` alias mapped to the current model for the opt-in period, and add header-based routing `Prefer-Model`. I can add support for `X-Model-Version` / `X-Model-Alias` quickly.

anya: Docs + SDK checklist: 1) warn in SDK when `model` is omitted (deprecation warning printed in dev logs), 2) update quickstart to show explicit pinning, 3) add a Breaking Changes page and deprecation template. I'll draft the SDK warning text. Suggestion for warning: "No model specified — the platform default will change on <date>. Pass `model` to pin behaviour."

jordan: From SRE/oncall POV: we need a canary rollout + automated alerts. If latency P95 rises >20% or error rate increases >1% in 30m, rollback. Canary phases: 5% -> 25% -> 100%. Also add a synthetic test that runs a fixed prompt set every minute to check tokenization deltas. :eyes:

sam: Sounds good. Tentative timeline I'm proposing: Week 0: announce + changelog and add deprecation headers in responses. Week 2: SDK warning in minor releases + alias created (`default-old`). Week 4: canary 5% then 25. Week 6: flip default; 2-week grace with alias still available. Week 8: remove alias. Does that seem reasonable?

maria: That timeline is reasonable. I'll own the public comms: email to workspace users, changelog, and a blog post. We should also loop in account managers for any enterprise customers who might be impacted.

liam: Plan for the runtime changes: add header parsing, alias routing, and a `compat-mode` flag. Quick snippet for the routing header we can support: 
```http
GET /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
X-Model-Version: v2
X-Model-Alias: default-old
```
This will let SDKs/clients request the old behaviour during the opt-in window. I'll open a PR with the header support and alias mapping.

anya: Draft comms copy (short): "Starting May 12 we will change the platform default model used when the `model` parameter is omitted. To avoid any change in behavior, set `model` in your requests or update to the latest SDK which will warn when `model` is not set. For enterprise customers we will send targeted notices. Deprecated alias `default-old` will be available until July 7."

sam: Who owns compatibility tests? We need CI + e2e checks to ensure top-level fields remain stable and to measure tokenization differences against a sample prompt set. @liam or eng-qa?

liam: I'll add runtime-level checks in CI to ensure API schema keys exist and types don't change. Please have eng-qa add smoke prompts so we can detect semantic/regression differences in outputs.

sasha: I'll add 10 representative prompts to the regression suite and run a weekly eval comparing tokenization and answer shape. I'll add a small gating job: if semantic drift > X we stop rollout.

maria: Action items: I will draft the announcement + coordinate with CX. Liam: add headers + alias. Anya: SDK warnings + docs. Sasha: regression prompts + eval. Jordan: canary config + alerts. Sam: coordinate final decision + signoff. I'll schedule an async review thread for the announcement copy.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout scheduled: 2026-05-10T14:00:00Z -> 5% for 48h (scheduled by liam)

sam: Great — please drop PR links and draft comms into this thread when ready. :thumbsup:
